{"id":"PKIX-vb4o","title":"pkix-path rejects PKITS 4.1.4 Valid DSA Signatures Test4 (DSA unimplemented)","description":"pkix-path: fail, 'signature not verified at chain index 0: unsupported signature algorithm'. PKITS ground truth says valid.

Not obviously a defect. pyca refuses it too ('Forbidden public key algorithm'); only OpenSSL accepts it. Refusing DSA in 2026 is a defensible deliberate choice, and two of three implementations make it.

The decision to record is whether pkix-path intends to never implement DSA, in which case this is a permanent known gap and should be named as one rather than sitting in the ground-truth disagreement list, or whether DSA verification belongs in the legacy tier alongside the SHA-1 verifiers from PKIX-qws.4 (verify-only, opt-in, outside the rustcrypto umbrella).

One of two remaining real ground-truth disagreements after PKIX-vcpy removed the 13 caused by unapplied policy inputs.","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-26T02:37:21.298490174Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-26T02:37:21.298490174Z"}

{"notes":"DECISION (2026-11-28, Mark): verify-only and opt-in. Nothing in this workspace signs with DSA, and no default or umbrella feature enables verifying it. The feature sits outside `default` and outside `rustcrypto`, exactly as rsa-sha1 and ecdsa-sha1 do, because that umbrella means 'algorithms we recommend'.

Rationale: FIPS 186-5 (3 Feb 2023) removed DSA as an approved algorithm, specifying RSA, ECDSA and EdDSA for generation and retaining DSA 'only for the purposes of verifying existing signatures'. NIST cited security analysis against DSA implementations and industry's move to ECDSA; the 186-4 transition ended 3 Feb 2024. Verification stays in scope because keys are facts -- a chain issued under DSA before it was retired either verifies or it does not, and a library that cannot say which is less useful than one that can. Refusing to generate is the part the standard settled.

Recorded in four places:
  AGENTS.md            '## Signature algorithms: DSA', Project stance (binding)
  README.md            '### Algorithm coverage'
  INTEROP.md           '## 8. PKITS DSA chains'
  pkix-path/src/lib.rs crate-level Limitations

This bead is therefore no longer a decision; it is implementation work. Scope when picked up:

1. A `dsa` feature on pkix-path, outside default and rustcrypto, with a DsaVerifier (RustCrypto's `dsa` crate).
2. RFC 3279 §2.3.2 domain-parameter inheritance -- a DSA key may omit p, q, g and inherit them from the issuer's certificate. DSA-only, the substance of PKITS 4.1.5, and the risky half: an implicit-state parse reaching outside the certificate under test.
3. Delete both entries from known_gaps() in pkix-difftest/tests/pkits_ground_truth.rs in the same change. That test fails if an exemption starts passing, so it cannot be left stale.

Found while recording this: README's '### Algorithm coverage' was substantially stale. It listed RSA-PSS, Ed25519 and P-521 as missing when all three ship and are enabled by rustcrypto, which is the default feature, and it described SHA-1 verifiers as 'intentionally not shipped' when rsa-sha1 and ecdsa-sha1 exist. pkix-path's own crate rustdoc carried the same wrong SHA-1 claim. Both corrected in the same commit; DefaultVerifier's dispatch table was read to confirm what it actually handles rather than trusting either doc."}
